sets.title: Two plants, two places
sets.summary: Students name what they see in a plant investigation, compare a plant grown in sunlight with one grown in the dark, and explain where to put a new plant, building cause language with because.

tasks.prompt: Look at the picture. A small plant is on the windowsill. Tell me what you see.
tasks.support: Words: plant, pot, leaves, sun, water, window.

visual.alt: A small green plant in a pot by a sunny window, next to a cup of water

models.text: Plant. Sun. Water.
models.note: Discourse: a short list. Sentence: no sentences yet. Word: three everyday nouns that name things in the picture.

models.text: I see a plant. The plant is green. It have a sun and a water cup.
models.note: Discourse: a few related ideas. Sentence: simple sentences that start with I see, The plant is and It, with an error in It have. Word: adds the color word green and the phrase water cup.

models.text: I see a little green plant in a pot by the window. The sun is shining on its leaves, and there is a cup of water next to it for watering.
models.note: Discourse: describes the scene from the plant outward. Sentence: a longer sentence joined with and, with clear detail. Word: precise words like shining, leaves and watering.

checklist: I named things in the picture.
I used a describing word, like green or little.
I spoke in a clear voice.

tasks.prompt: Now look at two plants. One plant grew by the sunny window for two weeks. One plant grew in a dark closet for two weeks. Tell how the plants are different. Then tell why they are different.
tasks.support: Use the words: taller, shorter, green, yellow, sunlight, because.

visual.alt: Two plants: a tall green plant by a sunny window and a short, pale plant in a dark closet

models.text: Window plant big. Closet plant small. Yellow. No sun.
models.note: Discourse: names the two plants one after the other. Sentence: short phrases without verbs. Word: size and color words carry the comparison.

models.text: The plant by the window is taller and green. The plant in the closet is short and the leaves is yellow. Because it don't get sun.
models.note: Discourse: compares, then gives a reason. Sentence: uses -er and because, but the because part stands alone and has errors (is, don't). Word: uses taller and leaves correctly.

models.text: The plant by the window grew taller, and its leaves are dark green. The plant in the closet is short, and its leaves look pale yellow. They are different because plants need sunlight to grow strong, and the closet plant did not get any light.
models.note: Discourse: describes both plants, then explains the cause in a clear order. Sentence: joins ideas with and and because in complete sentences. Word: exact words like pale, sunlight and grow strong.

checklist: I told how the plants are different.
I said why, using because.
I used science words like sunlight.

tasks.prompt: Your class wants to grow a new plant. Where should the class put it: by the window, in the closet, or on a shelf far from the window? Choose one place. Explain your choice using what you learned from the two plants.
tasks.support: I think we should put it ___ because ___. Last time, ___.

visual.alt: A new plant in a classroom with a sunny window, a closet and a shelf

models.text: Window. Sun good. Plant big.
models.note: Discourse: gives a choice and one idea. Sentence: short phrases. Word: everyday words like good and big stand in for a reason.

models.text: I think we put the plant by the window. Because the window plant was more big. The closet plant was yellow and small. So the window is better.
models.note: Discourse: states a choice, gives evidence and a conclusion with so. Sentence: some complete sentences, but more big and a stand-alone because show errors. Word: uses the colors and sizes from the test as evidence.

models.text: I think we should put our new plant by the window. Our test showed that the window plant grew taller and greener than the closet plant. That happened because it got sunlight every day. A shelf far from the window gets less light, so the plant might grow slowly. The window is the best place to help it grow.
models.note: Discourse: claim, evidence from the test, a reason, and a reason against another choice. Sentence: uses because, so and might to connect ideas. Word: precise words like greener, showed and less light.

checklist: I chose one place.
I used what happened to the two plants.
I said because to give my reason.
I said why another place is not as good.

sets.title: Amina's morning at school
sets.summary: Students describe a school morning, retell a classmate's morning routine in order with sequence words, and give an opinion with two reasons about how the class day should start.

tasks.prompt: Look at the picture of a school in the morning. Tell me what you see.
tasks.support: Words: bus, school, clock, book, friends.

visual.alt: A school bus in front of a school, a clock showing eight o'clock, and children walking in

models.text: Bus. School. Kids.
models.note: Discourse: a list of single words. Sentence: no sentences yet. Word: common nouns for what is in the picture.

models.text: I see a bus. The kids go in the school. The clock say eight.
models.note: Discourse: three separate ideas about the picture. Sentence: simple sentences with a verb, one missing -s (say). Word: adds the time and the action go in.

models.text: I see a yellow bus stopping in front of the school. Some kids are walking inside with their backpacks, and the clock says eight o'clock, so it is time to start the day.
models.note: Discourse: moves from the bus to the kids to the time and ends with a conclusion. Sentence: longer sentences joined with and and so. Word: details like stopping, backpacks and eight o'clock.

checklist: I named things in the picture.
I said what people are doing.
I spoke in a clear voice.

tasks.prompt: These pictures show what Amina does when she gets to school. Tell what she does, in order.
tasks.support: Use the words: first, next, then, last.

visual.alt: Three pictures in order: Amina gets off the bus, she sharpens her pencil, she reads a book with a friend

models.text: First bus. Pencil. Read book.
models.note: Discourse: names the steps in order. Sentence: phrases, not full sentences. Word: uses one sequence word, first, and simple nouns.

models.text: First Amina get off the bus. Next she go to class and sharpen her pencil. Then she read a book with her friend.
models.note: Discourse: tells all three steps in order. Sentence: complete sentences with first, next and then, but verbs are missing -s (get, go, read). Word: uses the action sharpen.

models.text: First, Amina gets off the bus and walks into the school. Next, she goes to her classroom and sharpens her pencil so she is ready to write. Then she sits on the rug and reads a book quietly with her friend until the morning meeting starts.
models.note: Discourse: a clear story of the morning with a beginning and an ending point. Sentence: correct verbs and added reasons with so and until. Word: exact words like classroom, quietly and morning meeting.

checklist: I told the steps in order.
I used first, next and then.
I said what Amina does in each picture.

tasks.prompt: Some students want to start the school day by reading quietly. Other students want to start the day with a math game. Which is the better way to start the day? Tell what you think and give two reasons.
tasks.support: I think ___ is better because ___. Also, ___.

visual.alt: A book for quiet reading and a computer with a math game, with a clock showing the start of the day

models.text: Book. I like. Quiet.
models.note: Discourse: a choice and a feeling. Sentence: one short memorized chunk, I like. Word: quiet is the only reason word.

models.text: I think reading is better. Because it is quiet and we can relax. Also I learn new words when I read it.
models.note: Discourse: an opinion with two reasons. Sentence: uses because, also and when, but the because part stands alone and read it has an extra word. Word: everyday words like relax and new words.

models.text: I think starting the day with reading is the better choice. First, reading is quiet, so it helps everyone calm down after a busy morning. Second, we learn new words every morning, and that helps us in all our subjects. A math game is fun, but it can get loud, so it might be better later in the day.
models.note: Discourse: opinion, two numbered reasons and a fair point about the other choice. Sentence: uses first, second, so and but to link ideas. Word: precise words like calm down, subjects and choice.

checklist: I told what I think.
I gave two reasons.
I used because or also.
I spoke in a clear voice.

sets.title: Finish the shape pattern
sets.summary: Students name and count shapes in a repeating pattern, explain what comes next, and judge a classmate's claim about the ninth shape, using math words like repeats and every third.

tasks.prompt: Look at the shapes in a row. Say the shapes you see. How many stars are there?
tasks.support: Words: star, heart, one, two, three, four.

visual.alt: A row of six shapes: star, star, heart, star, star, heart

models.text: Star. Heart. Four.
models.note: Discourse: names the shapes and gives a number. Sentence: no sentences yet. Word: shape names and a counting word.

models.text: I see star and heart. It have four star.
models.note: Discourse: names the shapes, then answers the question. Sentence: simple sentences with errors (have, star without -s). Word: uses the correct count.

models.text: I see stars and hearts in a row. There are four stars and two hearts, and the stars come in pairs.
models.note: Discourse: describes the row, counts both shapes and notices how they are grouped. Sentence: correct plurals and a sentence joined with and. Word: math words like in a row and pairs.

checklist: I named the shapes.
I said how many stars.
I used number words.

tasks.prompt: Here is the pattern: star, star, heart, star, star, heart. What shape comes next? Tell the shape and explain how you know.
tasks.support: Use the words: next, repeats, after, because.

visual.alt: The pattern star, star, heart, star, star, heart, then a question mark for the next shape

models.text: Star. Star, star, heart. Again.
models.note: Discourse: gives the answer and says the pattern. Sentence: words and phrases only. Word: again shows the idea of repeating.

models.text: Next is a star. Because it go star, star, heart and then again. The heart is the end so star come after.
models.note: Discourse: answer, then a reason. Sentence: uses because and so, with verb errors (go, come). Word: uses next, end and after.

models.text: The next shape is a star. The pattern repeats star, star, heart, and the last shape was a heart. That means the pattern starts over, so the next shape is a star, then another star, and then a heart again.
models.note: Discourse: answer, the rule of the pattern and a conclusion. Sentence: links ideas with that means and so. Word: math words like repeats, pattern and starts over.

checklist: I said the next shape.
I told how the pattern repeats.
I used because or so.

tasks.prompt: The pattern keeps going: star, star, heart, star, star, heart. Jae says the 9th shape in this pattern is a star. Do you agree or disagree with Jae? Explain your thinking.
tasks.support: I agree / I disagree because ___. Every ___ shape is a ___.

visual.alt: The start of the pattern star, star, heart, a question mark, and a student named Jae

models.text: No. Heart. Three, six, nine.
models.note: Discourse: disagrees and gives the counting as proof. Sentence: words only. Word: number words show the thinking.

models.text: I disagree with Jae. I count the shapes and number 9 is a heart. Because the heart is every three shape.
models.note: Discourse: position, then how the student checked, then a rule. Sentence: complete sentences with a stand-alone because and an error in three shape. Word: uses disagree and count.

models.text: I disagree with Jae. The pattern has three shapes in each part: star, star, heart. So a heart is always the 3rd, 6th and 9th shape. That means the 9th shape is a heart, not a star. Jae might have stopped counting at 8, and the 8th shape is a star.
models.note: Discourse: position, the rule, proof and a guess about why Jae made a mistake. Sentence: uses so, that means and might have. Word: exact words like 3rd, 6th, 9th and always.

checklist: I said if I agree or disagree.
I used the pattern to prove it.
I used order words like 3rd and 9th.
I explained my thinking out loud.
